questions.question: If the Reporting Verb is in Present or Future Tense, what happens to the tense of the Reported Speech?
questions.rationale: If the Reporting Verb is in Present or Future Tense, the tense of the Reported Speech does NOT change.

questions.question: In the SON rule for pronoun changes, what does the letter 'N' represent?
questions.rationale: In the SON rule, 'N' stands for 3rd Person (He, She, It, They), which undergoes No Change when converting narration.

questions.question: If the Reporting Verb is in Past Tense, what does 'Is/Am/Are' become in Indirect Speech?
questions.rationale: When the Reporting Verb is in Past Tense, 'Is/Am/Are' changes to 'Was/Were' in Indirect Speech.

questions.question: When the Reporting Verb changes from 'said to' to Indirect Speech, what does it become?
questions.rationale: 'Said to' becomes 'told' when converting to Indirect Speech with a Past Tense reporting verb.

questions.question: With a Past Tense reporting verb, what do 'Has/Have' become in Indirect Speech?
questions.rationale: Per the tense-change table, 'Has/Have' changes to 'Had' when the reporting verb is in the past tense.

questions.question: With a Past Tense reporting verb, how do 'Will/Can/May' change in Indirect Speech?
questions.rationale: 'Will/Can/May' change to 'Would/Could/Might' respectively when converting from direct to indirect speech with a past reporting verb.

questions.question: He said, "Two and three is five." → He said that two and three ___ five. Why does the tense stay 'is'?
options: Because the reporting verb is in present tense
Because it expresses a Universal Truth — the tense does NOT change (Rule 4)
It is incorrect; it must change to 'was'
questions.rationale: Rule 4 states that if the Reported Speech expresses a Universal Truth or Habitual Fact, the tense does not change — so 'two and three is five' keeps 'is'.

questions.question: For Yes/No questions converted to Indirect Speech, which connectors are used?
questions.rationale: Per Rule 5, the reporting verb 'said to' becomes 'asked', and 'if' or 'whether' is used as connector for Yes/No questions; question words (why, what, where) are retained for question-word questions.

questions.question: While converting narration, 'Tomorrow' changes to:
questions.rationale: Time-word changes: Today → That day, Yesterday → The previous day, Tomorrow → The next day.

questions.question: In the SON rule for pronoun changes, the letter 'O' stands for:
questions.rationale: In SON, 'O' means the 2nd Person (You) changes according to the Object of the reporting sentence.

questions.question: Choose the correct Indirect form: He said to me, "What is your name?"
options: He asked me what my name was.
He asked me what is my name.
He said to me that what was my name.
He asked me that what my name is.
questions.rationale: 'Said to' becomes 'asked', the question word 'what' is retained as connector, and the tense backshifts: 'is' → 'was' — hence 'He asked me what my name was.'
